reasoning: Circumfix negation ma + verb + -sh, as in ma ba3rafsh. Used in Palestinian speech, though urban Ramallah speakers often drop the -sh; the frame itself cannot be romanized cleanly, so ma-sh is given.
English loan block conjugated as a doubled Arabic verb: ballak, bballku. Widely used by young Palestinians.
MSA-origin noun used in everyday talk about the environment. Shadda on و. Some speakers say talawwus with s for ث.
Second of time is thaanye, with the kasra dropped before y; taa marbuta after ي is e. Many speakers say saanye with s for ث.
Palestinian eemta (also imta). Word-initial vowel seat is not written as a glottal. Alif maqsura is a.

romanization: illi bijri wara id-dinya ma bil7a'ha
vowelled_arabic: اللِّي بِجْرِي وَرَا الدِّنْيَا مَا بِلْحَقْهَا
reasoning: Palestinian dinya for dunya; 3rd-person b-imperfect contracts to bijri, bil7a'. ق is glottal in bil7a'ha.
The diphthong aw becomes oo: moosam, as in moosam iz-zeetuun, the olive season.
In colloquial speech ذ in this learned word is usually said z: jazzaab. Careful speakers say jadhdhaab.
b- present prefix with 2nd m. ti3raf; ween is the Palestinian where. The article slot assimilates to whatever noun follows.
Place name; the final hamza of صحراء is dropped in speech. il- assimilates to ص; nisba ending -iyye.

meaning_fix: fizzy / carbonated (as in mashruub ghaazi, soft drink)
reasoning: ghaazi is an adjective, carbonated; a soda is mashruub ghaazi, or just kola or gazooze in casual speech. On its own it is not really a noun for soda.
